NUTRITION
  calories: moderate deficit (approx. 10-15% below maintenance)
  protein: 1.6g per kg bodyweight daily
  carbs: moderate, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables)
  fats: moderate, focus on unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish)
  meal_frequency: 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks, consistent timing daily
  hydration: minimum 2L water daily
  avoid: added sugars, sugar-sweetened beverages, refined grains, high-saturated fat foods
  include: high-fibre foods (vegetables, legumes, whole grains), lean proteins (chicken, fish, tofu, eggs, Greek yogurt)
  pre_workout: small balanced meal 1-2h before training (e.g. Greek yogurt + berries, or boiled eggs + whole grain toast)
  post_workout: protein + fibre-rich carb (e.g. grilled chicken + quinoa salad, or cottage cheese + apple)
  monitor: blood glucose before and after exercise, adjust carbs if needed to prevent hypoglycaemia
  alcohol: limit or avoid
  sodium: moderate, avoid excess
  supplements: consider vitamin D and omega-3 if dietary intake is low (consult physician)
  notes: prioritize portion control, mindful eating, and regular meal timing to support glycaemic control and fat loss
  fasted_cardio_guidance: monitor blood glucose before and after fasted cardio; if <5.5 mmol/L, consume a small carb snack before; always carry fast-acting carbs during fasted sessions; avoid fasted cardio if feeling unwell or if blood glucose is low
  pre_fasted_cardio_breakfast:
    guidance: For most sessions, fasted cardio can be performed without breakfast if blood glucose is stable and above 5.5 mmol/L. If blood glucose is low or if she prefers to eat, choose a small, low-glycaemic, protein-inclusive snack.
    options:
      - Greek yogurt (unsweetened, 100g) + 6-8 almonds
      - 1 boiled egg + 1/2 small apple
      - Cottage cheese (low-fat, 100g) + 1/2 cup berries
      - 1 slice whole grain toast + thin spread of nut butter
      - 1 small protein shake (unsweetened, plant or whey) + 1/2 banana
    notes: Always check blood glucose before fasted cardio. If <5.5 mmol/L, eat one of the above options 20-30 minutes before exercise. Carry fast-acting carbs (e.g. glucose tablets) during cardio. Avoid high-sugar or high-fat foods pre-cardio.
  post_workout_snacks:
    options:
      - Greek yogurt (unsweetened, 150g) + 1/2 cup blueberries
      - Low-fat cottage cheese (100g) + 1 small apple
      - 1 small can tuna in water + 2 rye crispbreads
      - 1 boiled egg + 1 small orange
      - Protein shake (unsweetened, plant or whey) + 1/2 banana
      - 2 rice cakes + 2 tbsp hummus
      - 1 slice whole grain bread + 2 slices turkey breast
      - 1/2 cup edamame + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes
    guidance: Choose snacks with protein and fibre-rich carbs. Avoid added sugars and high-fat processed foods. Eat within 30-60 minutes post-exercise for best recovery and glycaemic control.
  cheat_meal:
    frequency: 1x per week
    guidance: Choose one meal per week to enjoy favourite foods in moderation. Preferably schedule after a workout. Avoid excessive portions, fried foods, and sugar-sweetened beverages. Monitor blood glucose before and 2 hours after the meal. Return to regular plan for next meal. If possible, include lean protein and vegetables with the cheat meal to help glycaemic control.
  intermittent_fasting:
    suitability: Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered for type 2 diabetes, but only with physician approval and careful monitoring due to risk of hypoglycaemia, especially when on metformin.
    recommended_protocols:
      - 12:12 (12 hours fasting, 12 hours eating window)
      - 14:10 (14 hours fasting, 10 hours eating window)
    guidance:
      - Begin with a 12:12 protocol and only progress to 14:10 if well-tolerated and blood glucose remains stable.
      - Do not skip meals after intense exercise or if feeling lightheaded, weak, or if blood glucose is <5.5 mmol/L.
      - Maintain 3 balanced meals within the eating window, including protein, fibre, and healthy fats at each meal.
      - Hydrate with water, herbal tea, or black coffee (no sugar) during fasting window.
      - Monitor blood glucose before, during, and after fasting periods, especially when starting IF.
      - Avoid fasting on days with high-intensity or long-duration exercise until tolerance is established.
      - Always carry fast-acting carbs in case of hypoglycaemia.
      - If any symptoms of low blood sugar occur, break the fast immediately with a balanced snack.
    not_recommended:
      - 16:8 or longer fasting windows without medical supervision
      - Skipping breakfast before fasted cardio or strength training if blood glucose is low
    consult: Discuss with healthcare provider before starting or modifying any fasting protocol.
